title: The Evolution of Reusable Ziplock Bags
summary: Single-use plastic bags have long been a staple in our daily lives, providing convenience but also posing significant environmental challenges.…
contentHtml:
Single-use plastic bags have long been a staple in our daily lives, providing convenience but also posing significant environmental challenges. These bags, made from non-biodegradable materials, contribute to pollution and harm ecosystems. However, as awareness of environmental issues grows, so does the demand for sustainable alternatives. This is where reusable ziplock bags step in, offering a solution that combines convenience with eco-friendliness.

What are zipper bags made of?

Ziplock bags are typically made of polyethylene, a type of plastic that offers flexibility, durability, and moisture resistance. Further, zipper bags can be made from low-density polyethylene (LDPE) and high-density polyethylene (HDPE). Many high-quality zipper bags from trusted suppliers are certified food-safe and can be used to store and preserve food items. Many manufacturers have recently begun making eco-friendly alternatives from biodegradable or compostable materials to address environmental concerns.

Exploring Ziplock Bag Sizes

There are different types of ziplock bags, including

  1. Slider bags

As the name suggests, slider bags have a sliding mechanism that facilitates easy opening and closing. It is usually made of plastic and is long-lasting.

  1. Pinch-and-seal bags

Pinch-and-seal or slider-free bags rely on the traditional mechanism of pinching and closing and don’t have a slider to seal the bag. The pinch and seal make the bag airtight and secure.

  1. Sandwich bags

Sandwich bags are specially designed to store sandwiches and other small deli items and are certified safe to come in contact with food.

  1. Stand-up bags

Stand-up bags or pouches come with a sturdy base that allows them to stand erect without support. These are typically common to store food items, spices, leaves, snacks, and more.

Stand-up bags are known for being stable and damage-resistant in comparison.

  1. Freezer bags

Freezer bags are built to withstand extreme cold temperatures and can be used to store & preserve food items such as meat and seafood.

  1. Gallon-sized bags

Gallon bags are larger than usual zipper bags and are suitable for storing bulkier items such as whole turkey and chicken.

  1. Anti-Static bags

Anti-static bags are built to store electronic items and protect against electrostatic discharge (ESD).

What are the different sizes of ziplock bags available?

Depending on the purpose it serves, ziplock bags can come in different sizes and shapes.

  • Small Size: Anywhere from 4-8 inches, for example, sandwich bags.
  • Medium Size: Typically 10-12 inches, for example, storing a variety of food items and general organization. They are also used as a travel pouch.
  • Large Size: Anywhere from 13-15 inches. Bulky food items or big articles.
  • Jumbo Size: Anywhere from 15-28 inches. They are used for storing bedding, blankets, etc. Many manufacturers also provide custom sizing for zipper bags.

Which Industries Benefit from Ziplock Bags?

Here are some common industries where ziplock bags are a staple.

  • Food Industry: To store and preserve food items, seafood, meat, poultry, sandwiches, and other deli items.
  • Retail outlets: For packing jewellery, stationary items, hardware, and electronics accessories.
  • Pharmacies & Healthcare sector: To store and safely organize medicines and small, blunt medical equipment.
  • Agriculture: To store seeds, cut leaves, dried flowers, etc.
  • Hospitality and Travel: To store handy items such as dental kits, toiletries, travel kits, soaps, etc.

Are Zip Bags Food-Safe?

Yes, zip bags that are certified food-safe can be used to store any edible items. Please note that not all ziplock bags get this certification and must be handpicked.

How to Clean  Reusable Ziplock Bags?

To keep your reusable ziplock bags clean and in good condition, it’s essential to practise proper maintenance and cleaning techniques. Start by rinsing the bags with warm, soapy water after each use to remove any residue or debris. For a deeper clean, you can wash the bags in the dishwasher or by hand with a mild detergent. Once clean, allow the bags to air dry completely before storing them to prevent mould or mildew growth.

Eco-Friendly Alternatives for Reusable Ziplock Bags

While reusable ziplock bags offer a sustainable option for reducing plastic waste, there are also non-plastic alternatives available. Materials such as silicone, cotton, or hemp can be used to create reusable bags that are durable, washable, and biodegradable. Brands like DKW  offer eco-friendly alternatives to traditional plastic bags, providing consumers with more choices for reducing their environmental footprint.

Conclusion

The evolution of reusable ziplock bags represents a positive step towards reducing plastic waste and adopting more sustainable consumption practices. By accepting reusable alternatives and making conscious choices in our daily lives, we can all play a part in protecting the environment for future generations. So next time you reach for a plastic bag, consider making the switch to reusable ziplock bags and join the movement towards a greener, more sustainable future.

Additional Reading

For more information on food-grade packaging and sustainable living, check out the following resources:

A Comprehensive Guide to Food Grade Packaging: Learn more about safe packaging materials for storing food.

5 Essential Commercial Uses of Resealable Ziplock Bags: Learn more about commercial uses of ziplock bags. 

By incorporating reusable ziplock bags into your daily routine and exploring alternative options, you can make a positive impact on the environment and contribute to a healthier planet for all.

These days, when environmental sustainability is more important than ever, businesses may help reduce waste and promote recycling. A key element of this effort is the recycling of Low-Density Polyethylene (LDPE), a type of plastic widely used in packaging and other products. In this article, we’ll look at the significance of LDPE recycling for businesses and the environment, as well as an overview of the LDPE recycling process and its advantages.

What is LDPE?

Low-Density Polyethylene (LDPE) is a thermoplastic made from ethylene monomers. It is known for its low density, flexibility, and resilience to moisture and chemicals. LDPE is widely used in packaging films, plastic bags, and a variety of consumer products due to its versatility and low cost.

Applications of Recycled Polythene

Recycled polythene has several applications in a variety of industries, helping to conserve resources and reduce waste.

  1. For Making Bags and Films
  • Various uses of recycled polythene bags

Recycled polythene bags are used for shopping, packing, and waste disposal. They provide a low-cost and environmentally beneficial alternative to typical plastic bags, lowering the use of virgin materials and minimizing environmental impact.

  • Applications of recycled polyethene films

Agricultural, construction, and packaging industries all use recycled polythene films. They protect against moisture, dust, and other environmental variables, making them excellent for crop protection, packaging, and product sealing.

  1. Usage in Various Industries

Recycled polyethene is widely used in many industries for a variety of applications:

  • Concrete slab coverings – Recycled polythene sheets are used to cover concrete slabs during construction to reduce moisture loss and maintain correct curing temperatures.
  • Food transport packaging – Recycled polythene is used to package and transport food products, preserving freshness and preventing contamination during travel.
  • Raincoats – Raincoats and waterproof clothes are made from recycled polythene, which protects against bad weather.
  • Nursing bags – Recycled polythene bags are used in hospitals and other healthcare facilities to store and carry medical supplies while maintaining hygiene and sanitation.
  • Plant floor covering (Agriculture) – Agriculture uses recycled polythene sheets to restrict weed growth, conserve moisture, and improve soil quality.
  • Nursery bags – Recycled polythene bags are used in greenhouses and gardening centres to pot and transplant seedlings and plants.

Importance of LDPE recycling for businesses and the environment

LDPE recycling is extremely important for both businesses and the environment. Recycling LDPE can save firms money because recycled components are frequently used to make new goods, eliminating the demand for virgin materials. Furthermore, implementing LDPE recycling can help a company’s reputation and attract environmentally concerned customers, increasing brand image and competitiveness.

From an environmental standpoint, LDPE recycling contributes to reducing the harmful impact of plastic waste on ecosystems. Recycling takes LDPE from landfills and incinerators, reducing pollution, conserving resources, and lowering greenhouse gas emissions connected with plastic production. Furthermore, recycling LDPE helps to promote the circular economy, in which materials are reused and repurposed to create a more sustainable and resource-efficient society.

Overview of the LDPE recycling process and its benefits

The LDPE recycling process normally includes collecting, sorting, cleaning, shredding, melting, and pelletization. LDPE materials are collected, sorted by type and colour, and then cleaned to remove contaminants. The sorted and cleaned LDPE is then shredded into smaller pieces before being melted and turned into pellets. These pellets can be used as raw materials to create a variety of goods, including bags, films, and other plastic items.

The benefits of LDPE recycling go beyond environmental conservation. Recycling LDPE minimizes the demand for fresh plastic production, which saves energy and resources during the manufacturing process. It also produces jobs in the recycling industry and boosts local economies. 

Furthermore, recycling LDPE helps to shut the loop on plastic waste, promoting a more sustainable and circular approach to resource management.

Other Waste Polythene Types

Specialty Applications

Recycled polyethene is used in specialized applications to meet specific needs and criteria.

  • Greenhouses using clear virgin polythene for tunnelling – Greenhouses made of clear virgin polythene provide temporary cover for crops, allowing for controlled growth conditions. However, these constructions have a short lifespan of approximately one year.

Benefits of Recycling LDPE

  1. Environmental benefits

Recycling LDPE offers several environmental benefits, including:

  • Reduced landfill waste – Recycling LDPE reduces waste disposal costs and pollution by diverting it from landfills.
  • Conservation of resources – Recycling LDPE protects natural resources such as oil and energy, which would otherwise be used to manufacture virgin plastic items.
  • Mitigation of pollution – Recycling LDPE reduces the release of toxic chemicals and greenhouse gases connected with plastic production and disposal, hence mitigating environmental pollution and climate change effects.
  1. Economic advantages for businesses

Recycling LDPE can generate economic benefits for enterprises, including:

  • Revenue generation – Businesses interested in LDPE recycling can earn money by selling recycled materials to manufacturers and other buyers, resulting in extra revenue streams.
  • Market competitiveness – Adopting LDPE recycling can boost a company’s market competitiveness by appealing to environmentally sensitive customers while also achieving sustainability standards.
  1. Contributions to sustainability goals

Recycling LDPE contributes to achieving sustainability goals by:

  • Promoting the circular economy: Recycling LDPE fosters a circular approach to resource management, where materials are reused and recycled, minimizing waste and maximizing resource efficiency.
  • Supporting corporate sustainability initiatives: Recycling LDPE aligns with corporate sustainability objectives aimed at reducing environmental impact, conserving resources, and promoting social responsibility.
  • Driving innovation and collaboration: Recycling LDPE encourages innovation in recycling technologies and collaboration among stakeholders to develop sustainable solutions for plastic waste management.

LDPE Recycling in Businesses

Implementing LDPE recycling in businesses involves several steps, including:

  1. Assessing LDPE usage and waste generation

Businesses have to analyze their LDPE usage and trash creation to identify options for recycling and waste reduction. This includes conducting waste audits, analyzing manufacturing processes, and estimating LDPE usage to establish baseline data for recycling initiatives.

  1. Setting up recycling programs

Businesses should set up recycling programmes to collect, separate, and process LDPE materials for recycling. This may include collaborating with recycling facilities, investing in recycling infrastructure, and giving employees training and materials to help them practise appropriate waste management.

  1. Educating employees and stakeholders

Educating employees and stakeholders is essential for the success of LDPE recycling programmes. Businesses can promote awareness about the necessity of recycling, provide trash segregation and recycling training, and encourage employee participation and engagement in recycling initiatives.

Challenges and Solutions

Despite the advantages of LDPE recycling, firms may face problems in launching and maintaining recycling programmes. Common challenges include:

  1. Common challenges in LDPE recycling
  • Contamination: LDPE materials can be contaminated with other materials or substances, which reduces their quality and recyclability.
  • Lack of infrastructure: Inadequate recycling infrastructure and facilities may reduce the availability and accessibility of LDPE recycling services.
  • Market demand: Fluctuations in market demand for recycled LDPE materials can have an impact on recycling enterprises’ pricing and profitability.
  1. Strategies for overcoming barriers

To overcome these challenges, businesses can adopt the following strategies:

  • Investing in technology: Investing in advanced recycling technology can increase the efficiency and effectiveness of LDPE recycling processes, hence improving material quality and market competitiveness.
  • Collaborating with stakeholders: Collaboration with government agencies, recycling organizations, and industry partners can assist firms in closing infrastructure gaps, expanding recycling networks, and generating synergies to meet common difficulties.
  • Promoting consumer awareness: Educating customers on the benefits of recycling LDPE and promoting products derived from recycled materials can boost demand for recycled goods and encourage recycling habits.
  1. Collaborative approaches to improve recycling rates

Collaborative approaches involving corporations, governments, and civil society are critical for increasing LDPE recycling rates and meeting sustainability targets. This may include:

  • Policy support: Governments can implement policies and regulations to encourage LDPE recycling, such as extended producer responsibility (EPR) programmes, landfill restrictions, and tax breaks for recycling efforts.
  • Public-private partnerships: Public-private partnerships can help fund recycling infrastructure, research and development of recycling technologies, and outreach and education campaigns to increase recycling knowledge and participation. 
  • Industry initiatives: Industry associations and consortia might lead collaborative efforts to standardise recycling procedures, share best practices, and foster innovation in LDPE recycling and circular economy solutions.

Conclusion

Finally, LDPE recycling proves essential for organizations looking to reduce their environmental effect, save money, and promote sustainability. Businesses may help to create a more sustainable future by recognizing the value of LDPE recycling, creating recycling programmes, and overcoming obstacles through collaborative methods and innovation. Businesses must prioritize LDPE recycling operations and adopt sustainable practices to protect the environment and secure long-term prosperity.

Recycling LDPE has environmental, economic, and social benefits, such as waste reduction, resource conservation, and pollution reduction. Businesses that recycle LDPE can reduce environmental impact, save money, and improve their reputation and competitiveness.

Businesses have an important role in promoting sustainability through LDPE recycling. Businesses that adopt recycling initiatives may demonstrate their commitment to environmental conservation, influence good change in the sector, and help to create a more sustainable and resilient future for future generations.

title: A Deep Dive into DKW Plastic Recycling
summary: Plastic recycling is the process of converting waste plastic materials into new goods while minimising waste and environmental effects. The…
contentHtml:
Plastic recycling is the process of converting waste plastic materials into new goods while minimising waste and environmental effects. The process begins with the gathering of used plastic objects such as bottles, containers, and packaging. These objects are then separated by category and colour, ensuring effective recycling. Plastic recycling is essential for preserving resources, lowering pollution, and fostering a more sustainable future.

Addressing plastic trash is critical to maintaining the environment and human health. Plastic pollution hurts wildlife, pollutes rivers and streams, and harms ecosystems. Recycling, limiting plastic consumption, and properly disposing of waste can help reduce these effects and build a cleaner, healthier planet for everyone.

Traditional recycling processes include collecting, sorting, and processing recyclable items such as plastic, paper, and glass. However, these technologies have limitations, such as high energy consumption, contamination, and restricted recyclability of some materials. Improving recycling technologies and promoting circular economy ideas are important for overcoming these issues.

Plastic Recycling in Sri Lanka

Sri Lanka is an island nation with a population of 21.4 million. Sri Lanka generates 7000MT of solid waste per day with the Western Province accounting for nearly 60% of waste generation. Western Province is the most populated province where the economic capital of Colombo is located. The highest waste generation is also recorded in the Western Province. The Colombo Municipal Council collects around 700800 tons of solid waste daily. The other Municipal Councils in the Metro Colombo Region comprising of Dehiwela-Mt. Lavinia Municipal Council (DMMC), Kolonnawa Urban Council (KUC), Sri Jayawardenapura Kotte Municipal Council (SJKMC) and Moratuwa Municipal Council (MMC) collect about 350- 400 tons of solid waste daily. The most common plastic waste products are straws, yoghurt cups, mega bottles, lunch sheets, milk packets, meal boxes, polyethene bags, sachet packets and wrappers. The Centre for Environmental Justice (CEJ) recently conducted several brand audits across the country.  These audits revealed that multi-national companies such as Coca-Cola, Unilever and Nestle contribute the most plastic pollution in Sri Lanka. However, the contribution from local brands also remains considerable. Around 50 % of the plastics that the world produces are single-use plastics, utilized for just a few moments, but remain on the planet for at least several hundred years.

Currently, Sri Lanka has over 400 companies engaged in plastic processing. A total sum of Rs.15 Bn has been invested in plastics re-processing in Sri Lanka. Almost 50% of this has come through Foreign Direct Investments. Out of this 66 % of this total investment is exclusively for the re-processing of plastic products for the export market. The main polymers for producing single-use plastics are HDPE, LDPE, PET, PP, PS, and EPS.2 The capacity of the local plastic processing industry at present is nearly 140,000 MT per annum with an annual average growth rate of around 10%. – 12%. 

The Stages of Recycling Plastic at DKW

Collection

This is the first stage of the recycling process, it involves the collection of recycling from homes, businesses, and schools. For this stage, everyone must correctly sort their plastic ready for collection and recycle all the items they can. 

The collection of plastic is key for the recycling system to operate well. The more plastic suitable for recycling that is collected the more material available to be reprocessed and used back into new products.

Sorting

The second stage is sorting plastic from other materials. Today, plastics are sorted for either mechanical recycling or landfill. Advanced recycling opens a new path for difficult-to-recycle plastics like chip bags and even artificial turf to be diverted to plastic recovery facilities.

Shredding and processing

A critical stage in recycling plastic is shredding or grinding plastic into smaller flakes. The washed and sorted plastic is sent through shredding machines where it is ground into smaller pieces of plastic.

The plastic is shredded in different manners depending on the classification and methods of the shredder.  Further sorting may take place to ensure a pure stream of material is produced. Plastics that are more difficult to recycle are sent to advanced recycling facilities.

Rebuilding

At an advanced recycling facility, the plastics are converted into liquid and gas molecules – the raw feedstock needed to make valuable new products.

New plastics

These building blocks can be used to create a variety of new products. 

Circular plastics

Certified-circular plastics are used in a variety of products, such as food-grade packaging. Once used, the products can be collected, sorted and recycled, helping to meet society’s goals for a more circular economy.

Challenges and Considerations

To achieve an effective and sustainable plastic recycling process, several problems must be overcome. Technical constraints, such as the complexities of separating different types of plastics and the energy-intensive nature of recycling, necessitate inventive solutions and technological breakthroughs. Regulatory difficulties and policy consequences are also important since governments must adopt effective recycling incentives and enforce recycled content standards. 

Furthermore, public awareness and education regarding plastic recycling are critical. Raising awareness through education programmes and accessible recycling infrastructure can help people make environmentally responsible decisions and contribute to a cleaner future. Collaboration among stakeholders is critical for addressing these difficulties and creating a circular economy in which plastics are reused and recycled efficiently.

Future Prospects and Innovations

Looking ahead, the future of plastic recycling seems positive, with innovative technologies leading the way. Chemical recycling, which breaks down polymers into their basic building blocks for reuse, is one example of an innovative approach to raising recycling rates and decreasing waste. 

Furthermore, advances in sorting and processing technologies improve recycling efficiency and cost-effectiveness. These inventions have huge scalability and adoption potential because they overcome significant difficulties in existing recycling systems. Research and development play an important role in driving these improvements, with ongoing efforts aimed at increasing recycling procedures, producing sustainable materials, and finding innovative solutions to plastic waste management.

By investing in research and development, we can open up opportunities for a more circular economy in which plastics are reused, recycled, and repurposed to reduce environmental impact.

Conclusion

Finally, plastic recycling is a vital solution for reducing the environmental impact of plastic waste and moving towards a more sustainable future. Its significance cannot be emphasised, as it saves resources, minimises pollution, and safeguards ecosystems. It is critical that stakeholders, including governments, organisations, and individuals, promote and invest in plastic recycling projects. We can maximise the potential of plastic recycling by prioritising recycling infrastructure, establishing effective laws, and encouraging innovation, resulting in a circular economy in which plastics are efficiently reused and recycled.

title: The Role of Food Safe Packaging in the Food Industry
summary: In the complex structure of the food sector, product safety and quality are important. This assurance is based on the…
contentHtml:
In the complex structure of the food sector, product safety and quality are important. This assurance is based on the concept of food grade and food safe packaging. In this blog article, we’ll look at how these terms are defined, why they’re important in the food sector, and how to negotiate the regulatory landscape. In addition, we will look at commonly used food packaging materials and discuss the importance of prioritizing food safety in packaging methods.

Definition of Food Grade and Food Safe Packaging

Food grade packaging refers to materials that are considered safe for direct contact with food. These materials must meet severe regulatory requirements to guarantee that they do not introduce any dangerous contaminants into the food they contain. Food safe packaging, on the other hand, covers a wider range of topics, focusing not just on the materials but also on the total safety of the packaging process, including handling and storage.

Importance of Food Safe Packaging in the Food Industry

The importance of safe food packing cannot be underscored. It provides the first line of defense against food contamination, spoilage, and degradation. It also serves an important role in maintaining the quality and freshness of food during transit, storage, and presentation. In the highly competitive food market, keeping consumer trust and confidence is critical, and food safe packaging provides visible assurances of product quality.

Understanding Food Grade Packaging

Food grade packaging refers to materials that have been specifically designed and manufactured to meet the demanding requirements for food contact. These materials must be non-toxic, resistant to chemical leaching, and suitable for a variety of food types. Let’s explore some examples of food grade packaging materials:

  • Food Grade Polythene Bags Sri Lanka: These bags are commonly used for packaging and storing food items in Sri Lanka, making sure they remain safe and fresh during transportation and storage.
  • Food Grade Containers for Shipping: Containers made from food grade materials are essential for shipping perishable goods, providing a secure and hygienic environment for the products.
  • Food Grade Cardboard Packaging: Cardboard boxes treated with food-safe coatings are widely used for packaging dry goods and non-perishable items, offering durability and eco-friendliness.
  • Food Grade Plastic Containers: Plastic containers manufactured from food grade plastics such as PP, LDPE or HDPE are suitable for storing a wide range of food products, from liquids to solids.
  • Food Grade Tin Containers: Tin containers lined with food grade coatings are ideal for packaging canned goods, offering protection against corrosion and contamination.
  • Food Grade Packaging Plastic Roll: Rollstock packaging made from food grade plastics is commonly used in automated packaging processes, providing a versatile and cost-effective solution.

Distinguishing Food Grade and Food Safe

While food grade and food safe packaging are closely related, it’s essential to understand the distinction between the two. Food grade refers specifically to the materials used in packaging, making sure they meet regulatory standards for food contact. On the other hand, food safety encompasses broader considerations, including the overall safety of the packaging process and its impact on food quality.

Regulatory Requirements and Certification in Sri Lanka

In Sri Lanka, as in many other countries, stringent regulatory requirements govern food grade packaging. These regulations aim to safeguard public health and ensure the integrity of food products throughout the supply chain. Obtaining food grade packaging certificates is essential for businesses involved in the production and distribution of food items, demonstrating compliance with regulatory standards.

Commonly Used Food Packaging Materials

Food packaging is made from a variety of materials, each with its own set of qualities and benefits. Plastic, paper, glass, metal, and biodegradable materials are among the most commonly used options. These materials must be carefully selected based on factors such as the type of food being packaged, environmental considerations, and regulatory compliance.

Importance of Food Packaging

The importance of food packaging extends far beyond mere containment. It serves as a vital tool in preserving food quality and safety, protecting against physical, chemical, and biological hazards. Additionally, food packaging plays a crucial role in facilitating transportation and distribution, enhancing shelf life, and providing consumers with essential information about the products they purchase.

Conclusion

To summarize, food safe packaging is the foundation of the food industry, ensuring the safety, quality, and integrity of food items from farm to fork. Businesses may develop trust and confidence in their products by knowing the differences between food grade and food safe packaging, following regulatory regulations, and putting consumer safety first. Making informed choices about food packaging and safety allows us to assist businesses that maintain the highest levels of quality and integrity. Let us continue to prioritize food safety throughout the food supply chain to ensure a healthier and more sustainable future.

Environmental Impact and Challenges

Plastics packaging in Sri Lanka has a significant impact on the environment, posing challenges related to plastic pollution, waste management, and sustainability. In Sri Lanka, the widespread use of plastic packaging has led to environmental concerns such as littering, marine pollution, and landfill accumulation. The disposal of plastic packaging, especially single-use plastics, contributes to land and water pollution, affecting ecosystems and wildlife. Efforts are underway in Sri Lanka to address these challenges through initiatives promoting plastic recycling, waste reduction, and the adoption of eco-friendly packaging alternatives. Furthermore, community events, workshops, and outreach programs can be organized to engage the public and encourage sustainable practices related to plastic packaging. Conclusion

As we walk towards a more sustainable future, it is essential for plastic packaging companies, manufacturers, and suppliers in Sri Lanka to prioritize eco-friendly practices, promote recycling, and explore innovative packaging solutions. contentHtml:
In the world of packaging, the collaboration between DKW Plastic Industries and Wijaya Products shows a strong, three-decade-long partnership. Our path is defined by our shared dedication to quality, innovation, and perfection in food-grade packaging solutions. Here’s a look back at how we helped Wijaya Products succeed by offering customized packaging solutions that have survived the test of time.

Proper packaging protects your food product from physical damage and chemical and microbiological contamination. Packaging is essential for preserving food quality, minimising food waste, and reducing preservatives used in food. If your products are not packaged properly, the packaging process can become a source of contamination or compromise.

This article narrative emphasizes the long-standing relationship and shared growth between DKW Plastic Industries and Wijaya Products, highlighting specific products that have been a part of this enduring partnership.

What is Food Grade Packaging?

Food grade packaging is a term used to describe the type of packaging that is safe for food products. This means that the material used to make the packaging is free from harmful chemicals and residues that could contaminate the food. Food grade packaging must meet certain standards to be classified as food safe.

Plastic packaging divides out from other materials used for food grade packaging due to its versatility, affordability, and ease. In places like Sri Lanka, where plastic manufacture is important in the packaging business, there is a rising focus on making food-grade plastic packaging. Plastic manufacturers in Sri Lanka are increasingly focusing on strict quality requirements to ensure that their goods meet food safety laws.

These plastic manufacturers in Sri Lanka use innovative technology and quality control techniques to create packaging that is not only long-lasting and efficient but also meets the necessary hygiene and safety standards for food contact. As the demand for packaged food grows, plastic packaging, particularly in Sri Lanka, plays an increasingly important role in guaranteeing the preservation and safe delivery of food goods to customers.

Food Safety Management Systems (ex: ISO 22000 , or the Global BRC / IOP category B food contact standard for food packaging and other packaging materials) have been developed to ensure the safe and hygienic manufacturing of packaging that comes into contact with food. These standards are being adopted worldwide by packaging manufacturers to help improve their manufacturing facilities and ensure the best quality and hygienically manufactured packaging is available. IFS PACsecure provides HACCP based food safety for packaging material guidelines to food producers/packagers.

Partnership Overview: DKW and Wijaya Products

DKW has been in partnership with Wijaya Products for over 30 years. In this article let’s look back at how DKW Plastic Industries helps Wijaya products succeed by offering LPDE food packaging, PP food packaging and HPDE outer and inner bags. 

  • LPDE Food Packaging

For years, Wijaya Products has trusted DKW Plastic Industries to provide the quintessential salt bag — a staple in every kitchen. Our LDPE food-grade bags have grown to meet Wijaya’s expanding needs, providing customizable dimensions and durability that have become synonymous with the Wijaya brand.

  • PP Food Packaging

DKW’s polypropylene reel forms have been instrumental in packaging a variety of Wijaya’s food products. These reels are more than simply packing materials; they reflect the efficiency and dependability that have helped Wijaya maximize its production lines, and boost productivity and product freshness.

  • HPDE Outer and Inner Bag

Our HDPE bags have been the packaging choice for Wijaya’s bulk noodle products, showcasing our ability to provide robust and safe packaging solutions. These bags have safeguarded the quality and taste of Wijaya noodles, reaching countless consumers in perfect condition.

Advantages of Food Grade Packaging for Wijaya Products

  • Protection and Hygiene

The main obvious benefit of food grade packaging for Wijaya Products is food protection and safety. The food will be protected from harmful microorganisms that will decrease the food’s quality. This will not just protect the food from the organisms not perceived by the naked eye, but this will also protect the food from insects, rodents, and other pests that will most likely contaminate the food as well.

Food grade packaging also protects the food from temperatures – heat and cold – that can be harmful to the food, depending on the type. Moisture and oxygen can somehow affect the food’s quality, too. Rest assured, food inside great food packaging products is safe and protected.

Last, but not least, food grade packaging prevents damage to the food during the shipping, delivery, and handling process.

  • Preservation and Long Shelf Life

While the clear benefit of food grade packaging is a way to protect the food from contaminants, it should also be obvious that this can preserve food. This will prolong the food’s shelf-life. For example, certain foods discolour, grow mould, and spoil when exposed to air. Food packaging products will be able to protect the food from too much air exposure, thus prolonging its shelf life. That is what the retail packaging and every food packaging is for – prolonging the shelf life.

  • Communication

Now, this is important. A food packaging product can establish a “communication” between the food and the consumer. For example, the food packed in its original package at the store will have a label, nutrition facts, ingredients, expiration date, and any other information that a consumer needs to know. Another example is at home. When you store your food in a specific container, you will often label it with the name and the date that you placed it on the container to avoid confusion when you are ready to consume the food.

Ensuring Compliance and Quality Assurance

Quality assurance is crucial for food processors to ensure the safety, integrity, and consistency of their products. Implementing effective quality standard operating procedures (SOPs) is essential to meet regulatory requirements, maintain customer satisfaction, and protect brand reputation. In this section, we will discuss the essential SOPs that food processors should consider implementing to uphold high-quality standards in their operations.

  1. Incoming Raw Material Inspection: Thoroughly inspecting and testing incoming raw materials is a critical SOP to ensure the quality and safety of ingredients. Establish protocols for visual inspection, sampling, and testing to verify compliance with specifications and prevent the entry of contaminated or substandard materials.
  2. Equipment Calibration and Maintenance: Regular calibration and maintenance of processing equipment are vital for accurate measurements, consistent performance, and adherence to quality standards. Develop SOPs to schedule and document calibration, maintenance, and repairs to minimize equipment-related issues and ensure reliable operations.
  3. Cleaning and Sanitation: Robust cleaning and sanitation procedures are essential to prevent cross-contamination, microbial growth, and foodborne illnesses. Establish detailed SOPs for cleaning and sanitizing equipment, utensils, and processing areas, including proper use of cleaning agents, frequency of cleaning, and verification methods.
  4. Product Formulation and Recipe Control: Accurate product formulation and recipe control are crucial for consistent product quality. Develop SOPs to ensure precise measurement of ingredients, proper mixing procedures, and detailed batch record keeping to maintain product consistency and traceability.
  5. Packaging and Labeling: Proper packaging and labelling procedures are essential for consumer safety and compliance with regulatory requirements. Establish SOPs for accurate and compliant packaging, including allergen labelling, nutrition facts, ingredient declarations, and product identification.

Conclusion

Throughout the years, DKW Plastic Industries has not only supplied Wijaya Products with packaging materials but has also ensured that these materials meet the highest standards of food safety, as mandated by government certification. Our dedication to adapting and customising our products to fit Wijaya’s evolving requirements has been a cornerstone of our service.

As we reflect on this enduring partnership, we recognize that our shared values and dedication to customer satisfaction have been key to our collective growth. We look forward to continuing this journey with Wijaya Products, as we explore new horizons and innovative packaging solutions in the food industry.

By upholding our commitment to sustainability and quality, DKW Plastic Industries remains at the forefront of the packaging industry, ready to face the challenges of the future alongside our esteemed partner, Wijaya Products.

title: 5 Essential Commercial Uses of Resealable Ziplock Bags

contentHtml:
Resealable ziplock bags are a flexible and cheap packaging alternative for food and non-food goods. This packaging is perfect for different types of markets, including jewelry, spare parts, manufacturing, office organization, medical storage, and home use.

Resealable ziplock bags are resealable plastic bags with a zipper that can be opened and closed several times. Reusable zip bags are useful for storing a wide variety of things, saving businesses money and helping the environment.

In this blog post, we will walk you through everything you need to know about resealable ziplock bag packaging and the various commercial uses of this type of packaging.

Hospitals: Sterile Storage Solutions

Plastics are important to guarantee the safety of health workers and patients. Plastics maintain and secure medical devices safely and inert so that they don’t interfere with the medicinal system. In exchange, these medical devices do not expose us to illnesses and diseases. Ziplock bags help store sterile medical supplies and equipment. They help to secure biohazardous materials before disposal. Ziplock bags transfer and preserve tissue samples for laboratory processing.

DKW Plastics produces high-quality medical bags in a variety of shapes and sizes, depending on their intended use and contents. 

Garages

We can use resealable ziplock bags in garages to store sharp metal parts, screws, nails, and so on. These resealable ziplock bags increase productivity in car repair settings. Bolts are neatly organized and kept in resealable ziplock bags to prevent misplacing or forgetting. 

These resealable zip bags extend the life and functionality of auto repair parts by shielding them from dust and moisture. Car spare parts in Sri Lanka are stored in resealable ziplock bags, which facilitates finding them during repairs and minimizes downtime.

If you are interested in knowing more about our resealable ziplock bags, and their sizes, or need to share your requirements, you can contact our team via contact form submission.

Jewelry Shops

Jewelry shops put the jewelry in ziplock bags silicone in a compact and precise manner to keep it from getting lost. This ensures that even the smallest jewelry is securely stored in a ziplock bag, which can form an airtight seal. The airtight seal keeps out dust and other environmental pollutants that could alter the jewelry’s composition. 

Elements like oxygen and sulfur are the major cause of rust in metal jewelry and tarnish in gold. Lots of small e-commerce businesses that sell handmade jewelry use zip lock bags as inner packaging when shipping to their customers. Ziplock bags are ideal for shipping jewelry orders and safeguarding costly gemstones, gold, and silver from scratches.

Garments: Fashion Forward Packaging

Ziplock bags are a great way to pack clothes. They’re easy to use, lightweight, and easy to carry. Ziplock bags are leak-proof, making them perfect for storing delicate clothes. They can also be reusable, saving money and protecting the environment. Garments use resealable ziplock bags to maintain the freshness of the clothes. These zip bags help to protect delicate fabrics from dust, and moisture. Because of this, the ziplock bags help in labeling clothing samples for easy reference in the showroom.

Food Manufacturing: Hygienic Packaging Solutions

People have been using different types of resealable packaging for food packaging. It helps to safely seal and preserve ingredients for batch production. Ziplock bags help to package and seal individual portions of snacks or condiments. Zip bags ensure the freshness and safety of food products during storage and transport. Ziplock bags can extend shelf life and reduce waste.

Conclusion

In today’s daily use, you can use ziplock bags for different commercial uses, including hospitals, garages, jewelry shops, garments, and food manufacturing. They prevent the stored items from coming into direct contact with the air and help keep them clean, dry, and fresh for a long period. These bags offer convenience and reusability with their zipper closure mechanism. There are three types of ziplock bags in our product list. They are plain ziplock bags, custom printed ziplock bags, and kidney handle ziplock bags. The material is LDPE. Our ziplock bags have customizable features like patch handles and printed artwork creating a perfect fit for your requirements.

contentHtml:
There are different types of materials available for food packaging. Each packaging material has advantages and disadvantages. We’ll help you get the packaging you need to serve your food safely and responsibly as Sri Lanka’s top food packaging experts.

DKW Plastics offers a variety of high-quality packaging products to keep your food safe. Whether you’re a small business owner or a large-scale retailer, our resealable ziplock bags, food grade packaging, garment packaging, gusset bags, multi-color polythene reels, and retail & wholesale bags are designed to meet your unique food packaging needs. Visit our shop today to explore our wide range of food packaging products.

What is food grade packaging?

Food grade packaging refers to a type of packaging that is suitable for food goods. This indicates that the packaging is free of dangerous chemicals and substances that might harm the food. To be classified as food safe, food grade packaging must meet specific standards.

Benefits of Food Grade Packaging for Your Products

·   Protects the Food

When your food goods are ready to be shipped and delivered to stores, they will be handled by various people. These edible products are protected from breakage and dangerous infection by food grade packaging. It also safeguards the food against moisture, oxygen, and temperature changes.

·   Preserves Freshness

The main advantage of food grade packaging is that it helps in the preservation of the quality and freshness of your food products. Everything from baked loaves of bread to salty snacks and delightful desserts can now have a longer shelf life while remaining delicious to eat.

·   Professional Appearance

Furthermore, food grade packaging offers your goods a more professional appearance, which can assist in raising sales and attracting more customers. You may also personalize the food-safe package with your company’s colors and representation to make it even more distinctive.

Examples of food-grade plastics

Low-density polyethylene (LDPE)

LDPE is the least-priced plastic film material. It is soft, flexible, transparent, and smooth, with good moisture resistance, breaking down, and chemicals. It is most typically found in plastic bags, but it is also used extensively in squeezable food bottles, bread and frozen food packing, and flexible lids.

Polypropylene

Most PP is translucent rather than transparent, allowing light to pass through but preventing clear vision. Polypropylene is a low-cost material with outstanding optical clarity and gloss.

These plastic bags are also FDA certified and have good chemical hardness and durability. Furthermore, polypropylene bags are brighter than LDPE or LLDPE bags, allowing for better quality products.

High-density polyethylene (HDPE)

HDPE is the most common polyethylene film used in food packaging. It is semi-translucent and highly resistant to solvents. HDPE is the least flexible and strongest of the polyethylene films, making it ideal for applications requiring shape retention. HDPE can be found in water, juice, and milk bottles, margarine and butter tubs, cereal box liners, and retail and supermarket bags.

The Impact of Food-Grade Packaging on Food Safety

Prevention of Contamination

As with any kind of foreign material, detecting the problem before the product reaches consumers is the first and best line of defense. Failing to discover contaminated materials, and allowing them to reach the shelves, can have costly and disastrous consequences. In addition to lost consumer confidence, contaminated foods can lead to costly recalls and lawsuits.

X-ray food inspection is one of the most effective forms of foreign contamination detection available today. In addition to detecting contaminants, X-ray inspection can detect container defects, missing components, and incorrect fill levels.

While packaging does not pose the greatest threat to food contamination, it still requires monitoring to ensure that consumers are getting a safe product every time.

Preservation of Freshness and Flavor

To keep a food product crisp and fresh, the package must provide a barrier to moisture. Food changes such as off-flavor and rancidity may occur if the packaging material has a poor oxygen barrier, allows gas permeation, and allows passage of light to the food.

Salt, sodium nitrite, spices, vinegar, and alcohol have been used to preserve foods for centuries. Sodium benzoate, calcium propionate, and potassium sorbate are used to prevent microbial growth that causes spoilage and slow changes in color, texture, and flavor.

Role in Extending Shelf Life

Modified atmosphere packaging, or MAP, involves the use of a gas atmosphere in a packaged food to extend shelf life, typically consisting of an inert gas such as nitrogen and an antimicrobial active gas such as carbon dioxide.

The right selection of packaging materials and technologies maintains product quality and freshness during distribution and storage.

Selecting the Right Food-Grade Packaging for Your Product

Here is a list of important considerations for successfully selecting your food grade packaging:

·   Consideration of Packaging Material

When it comes to the packaging materials you choose to package your product, it’s a good rule of thumb to treat your products like you would treat yourself. Just as you would not want to live in a home that is too big or too small, the right space for the right package has a great effect on the result.

So why is food grade plastic good for your packaging material? Food grade plastic is designed to be safe for storing and packaging food, but it’s important to note that all plastics, including food grade plastics, can potentially leach harmful chemicals into food or beverages, especially when exposed to heat or acidic conditions.

·   Matching Packaging to Product Type

When it comes to the matching packaging you have to match the packaging type according to your product type. The right packaging will give your product a longer shelf life.

·   Sustainability Factors

Sustainable food packaging is about reducing the environmental footprint of packed food. Innovative sustainable packaging aims to reduce food waste and loss reduction by improving food quality, as well as food safety issues such as food borne diseases and food chemical contamination.

All of these are important things to consider when selecting the best food grade packaging for your product.

Considerations when Choosing Food Safe Packaging

When selecting a food grade packaging material, keep in mind the intended purpose of the product as well as how your customer may utilize the product. Consider:

·   What kind of food-safe material will the package be composed of?

·   What kind of food is going to be packaged? Is it going to corrode the packaging?

·   Is the packaging still food safe if hot food is placed within it or cooked within it?

·   Will your packaging choice affect the product’s shelf life?

·   What kind of environmental circumstances will the food and packaging face?

·   What will happen to the packaging?

·   How much will packaging and shipping cost?

·   Will the package be stackable and able to handle stacking weight?

·   Is there a barrier in place to protect the food from contamination and spoilage?

Package Your Food Products at DKW Plastics Products

Need food grade packaging? At DKW Plastics we manufacture and stock a large range of food grade packaging that can be customized to suit your needs. Contact us at (051) 222-2117 to place an order or inquire now online.

Conclusion

To improve their performance and safety, food-grade plastics may require the inclusion of specialized additives. Stabilizers, antioxidants, colorants, and antimicrobial compounds are examples of additives that can be used to prevent bacterial development. The polymerized material is subsequently formed into the appropriate shape using extrusion or injection molding machinery, such as sheets, films, bottles, containers, or other packaging materials.

Finally, food-grade plastics are rigorously tested to guarantee that dangerous chemicals or impurities do not leak into food. This includes migration, chemical resistance, and thermal stability studies.
